Passkey ceremony recordings

Help test crypto/passkey, a proposed Go standard library package for signing in with passkeys.

This page runs a few WebAuthn ceremonies with your browser and authenticator, and records exactly what they produce, so the package can be tested against real devices rather than simulations.

Nothing personal is recorded: the account is a random ID made up for this session, and the passkey you create is for this site only. Delete it afterwards if you like.

Model, firmware, provider app, whether a PIN is set, anything unusual. The browser and OS are recorded automatically.

By continuing, you dedicate the recording this session produces to the public domain under CC0 1.0. It will be published, so anyone can use it as a test vector.

Session

Everything you do is saved as you go, so if you stop halfway, what you did still helps. See the recording at any point.

This session records a conditional registration: a passkey created automatically, without prompting, right after you sign in with a password your password manager filled in. Whether it happens is up to whatever handles passkeys on this page: the browser's own manager (Google Password Manager in Chrome, Apple Passwords in Safari), a third-party provider on iOS or macOS, or a browser extension like 1Password that takes over WebAuthn calls and can apply its own policy. Any answer is a useful recording. It works in two steps, each a real form submission.

1. Save a password. Submit this form and accept your browser's offer to save the password.
2. Sign in with it. Let the browser's password manager fill the password (don't type it), then submit. The page will then immediately ask the browser to create a passkey without prompting you.
  1. Create a passkey

    A registration with user verification preferred. Follow whatever your browser and authenticator ask.

  2. Sign in

    A login with user verification preferred. Pick the passkey you just created.

  3. Sign in again, with allowCredentials

    The same, but the site names the credential it expects, as it would for a re-authentication prompt in a signed-in session.

  4. Sign in requiring user verification

    A login with user verification required. Your browser may ask you to set up a PIN, or refuse: either is a useful result. Do this one last, as it can change your authenticator.

  5. Optional: sign in from the autofill suggestions

    A login through the autofill (conditional UI) path. Click the button, then click into the field and pick the passkey from the suggestions.

Thank you. Anything to add? Edit the notes.

If a password manager fills passwords for you in this browser — the built-in one, or an extension like 1Password — you can also record a conditional registration: the silent passkey creation some of them do right after a password sign-in. It's the rarest example we need. Two more minutes.

Have another authenticator? Start another session.

Recordings are collected for crypto/passkey by Filippo Valsorda; contributors submit them under CC0, and they are published. This site is testdata/_capture in filippo.io/passkey.
